S067.name: Preoccupation_with_Appearance
S067.description: Preoccupation with one or more perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance that are not observable or appear slight to others.

subtypes.Skin Defects: Excessive preoccupation with practically invisible acne, scars, or complexion.
subtypes.Facial Features: Preoccupation with the shape or size of the nose, eyes, or mouth, which appear normal to others.
subtypes.Asymmetry: Excessive obsession with the face or body not being perfectly symmetrical.
subtypes.Muscle Dysmorphia: The belief that one's body is too small or insufficiently muscular despite being normal or muscular.
subtypes.Specific Body Parts: Obsession that specific parts like hair, teeth, or chest are ugly or abnormal.

S068.name: Appearance_Related_Repetitive_Behaviors
S068.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to appearance concerns.

subtypes.Mirror Checking or Avoidance: Compulsively checking oneself in the mirror frequently or, conversely, avoiding mirrors strictly.
subtypes.Excessive Camouflaging: Spending excessive time and effort to hide perceived flaws using makeup, clothes, hats, or sunglasses.
subtypes.Skin Picking: Picking or manipulating the skin excessively to remove or 'fix' flaws.
subtypes.Reassurance Seeking: Repetitively asking others for confirmation that one's appearance is okay or not strange.
subtypes.Comparing: Constantly comparing one's body parts with those of passersby or celebrities.
subtypes.Seeking Cosmetic Procedures: Repeatedly seeking or receiving plastic surgery or dermatological procedures.

patient_info.stressor: Sunita’s firm won a regional sustainability award for one of her community-scale projects, bringing public recognition that included photographs, interviews, and a panel appearance in front of peers and clients. Instead of experiencing the achievement as purely validating, she became increasingly absorbed by a perceived defect in her appearance that others did not see as significant, and her usual architectural precision shifted into repeated mirror checking, photo reviewing, and attempts to control how she would be seen in professional and family settings. Over time, the preoccupation severely disrupted her work: she delayed presentations, avoided networking tied to the award, and spent so much energy preparing her appearance that project deadlines and family gatherings suffered. After she cancelled an important client presentation at the last minute, her husband and a trusted colleague helped her arrange an urgent outpatient psychiatric consultation.

S067.name: Preoccupation_with_Appearance
S067.description: Preoccupation with one or more perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance that are not observable or appear slight to others.
S067.manifestation: I’m here because I can’t stop seeing this droop and unevenness around my mouth and jaw in every photo and reflection, and even when people tell me I look fine, it feels so obvious that I’ve started avoiding presentations and clients.

S068.name: Appearance_Related_Repetitive_Behaviors
S068.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to appearance concerns.
S068.manifestation: Before work or any family event I can spend hours checking the bathroom mirror, taking phone pictures from different angles, redoing my makeup and scarf, asking my husband if my face looks lopsided, and then scrolling through other women’s photos to see how bad mine looks beside theirs.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: I cancelled a major client presentation at the last minute and have been missing award-related networking because I can’t face being seen, and my project deadlines and family gatherings have started to fall apart around this.
